title: AWS FinOps Agent
subtitle: Reproducible cost insight → owned action
scenario: 41% synthetic storage-cost increase, reconciliation and engineering handoff

slides.title: AWS FinOps Agent
slides.takeaway: Cost queries and recommendation follow-up require source reconciliation and ownership.
slides.notes: The entire FinOps Agent service remains preview. This presentation focuses on the daily engineering value: cost explanation, anomaly investigation, recommendation triage and reporting. It does not grant infrastructure or purchasing authority. The illustrative storage-cost demo uses synthetic numbers to teach reconciliation; it is not an account result or a measured saving.
slides.outcome: Question → reconcile → investigate → prioritize → hand off
slides.label: FinOps / Platform engineering / Service owners

slides.title: Use case · explain a 41% storage-cost increase
slides.takeaway: A useful answer separates observed movement, likely drivers and unresolved uncertainty.
slides.notes: Use two complete 14-day periods and the same account, Region and cost basis. The 41 percent figure is an illustrative calculation used in the demo, not a real anomaly from the user’s account. Determine which service or usage type moved before proposing a cause. CloudTrail correlation can inform a hypothesis when access is configured, but time proximity alone does not establish causality.

items.title: Scope
items.body: Accounts, complete periods, cost basis and dimensions.

items.title: Reconcile
items.body: Repeat the material total in the source cost view.

items.title: Investigate
items.body: Separate usage, rates and correlated change evidence.

items.title: Hand off
items.body: Assign a bounded action and post-change measurement.

slides.title: FinOps capability groups and output types
slides.takeaway: The service helps analyze and route work; it does not apply resource changes.
slides.notes: The capability map is an analytical workflow: understand spend, investigate anomalies, retrieve optimization opportunities, produce reports, run tasks and route results. All are within the preview service. Recommendation output comes from connected cost-management sources and must not be presented as a second independent optimizer or a completed change. The native collaboration writes are explicit and limited.

items.title: Cost inquiry
items.body: Breakdowns, comparisons, forecasts and commitment views.

items.title: Anomaly investigation
items.body: Rank cost drivers; inspect usage versus rates.

items.title: Reports
items.body: HTML, PDF and editable PowerPoint artifacts.

items.title: Jira / Slack
items.body: Configured issues, comments and outbound updates.

slides.title: Data permissions determine analytical depth
slides.takeaway: Context adds business meaning; it does not grant access to missing sources.
slides.notes: Create the agent and operator access paths and activate the cost services needed for the pilot. Cost Explorer supplies cost and usage views; anomaly and optimizer services provide their own evidence. CloudTrail access can add change context. If a source is not permitted, the corresponding analytical depth is unavailable. The account-to-owner mapping is interpretive context, not a permission policy.
rows: Spend, usage, trends and commitment views
Enable and scope the required API access
Enable the relevant services and permissions
Optional access and reviewed context files

slides.title: Record comparable cost-query definitions
slides.takeaway: Acceptance: reconcile one material total using identical source filters.
slides.notes: A cost narrative is only reproducible when the time range, grouping, filters and cost basis are explicit. Choose complete periods for the demonstration to avoid treating a partial day as a trend. Reconcile at least one material total in the source view before sharing a report. Do not use an account-specific answer outside its documented scope.
inputs: Service, Region, tag dimensions and cost basis
actions: Retrieve accessible cost and usage data
Compare periods and produce relevant breakdowns
outputs: A numerical explanation with its query scope
Follow-up questions grounded in the same context

slides.title: Forecasts and commitments inform a decision
slides.takeaway: Acceptance: a forecast is not a guaranteed bill, and a recommendation is not a purchase.
slides.notes: This capability helps the team understand expected spend and current commitment usage. Make the analysis period and assumptions visible. A recommendation may reflect a source service’s model and eligibility rules, and it still requires review against business constraints. Keep purchasing decisions with the authorized finance or platform owner. No commitment purchase is demonstrated here.
inputs: A named period and relevant usage assumptions
actions: Retrieve supported purchase or commitment recommendations
outputs: Candidates for finance and engineering review

slides.title: Separate observed cost changes from causal hypotheses
slides.takeaway: Acceptance: label correlated changes as hypotheses until the causal mechanism is verified.
slides.notes: An anomaly investigation should answer what moved and how much before answering why. Higher usage, higher rates and mixed effects lead to different actions. When CloudTrail is available, compare candidate events with the service and cost timeline. A nearby change can be relevant without being the cause. Capture what additional evidence would distinguish the leading hypotheses.
inputs: A detected anomaly and the affected cost slice
actions: Rank contributors and separate rate/usage movement
Search for operational activity correlated with the change

slides.title: Demo · reconcile the storage-cost anomaly
slides.takeaway: Work from a labeled synthetic fixture, then demonstrate the source-reconciliation method.
slides.notes: The bundled synthetic fixture has fourteen baseline rows at $100 each, totaling $1,400, and fourteen comparison rows at $141 each, totaling $1,974. The difference is $574, or 41%. It deliberately contains no account, usage-type, quantity or rate breakdown, so it supports arithmetic reconciliation only—not driver attribution or a causal conclusion. These figures are invented for instruction. For an authorized real analysis, use matching date windows, filters and cost basis, then obtain the additional breakdown and event evidence. Any real Jira write still requires the configured approval.
slides.prompt: Reconcile synthetic totals of $1,400 and $1,974 (41% higher). This fixture cannot establish drivers. For authorized real data, match periods and cost basis before testing usage, rate and change hypotheses. Do not modify infrastructure.
steps: Fix complete periods, account scope, service grouping and basis.
Reconcile the fixture totals; require source breakdowns for any driver claim.
Inspect usage and rate evidence instead of inferring from spend alone.
Compare a candidate change with evidence and alternative explanations.
Draft an owned follow-up and inspect the Jira confirmation boundary.
slides.success: A reproducible explanation and a bounded next step; no infrastructure mutation or claimed realized savings.
slides.preflight: Use sanitized authorized cost access or the bundled synthetic fixture. Any real Jira write needs the configured confirmation.
slides.fallback: The included fixture is sufficient to teach the method offline; it must remain visibly labeled synthetic.

slides.title: Prioritize existing optimization recommendations
slides.takeaway: Acceptance: estimated monthly savings are not realized savings; the team executes changes separately.
slides.notes: The agent makes optimizer results easier to triage. Select reversible opportunities that fit the team’s operational constraints rather than sorting only by the largest estimate. Check utilization evidence, performance requirements and existing commitments. The generated ticket is the start of an engineering process. Measure results after an approved change using a comparable period, and do not double-count overlapping recommendations.
inputs: Cost Optimization Hub and Compute Optimizer results
Owned resources, risk constraints and savings thresholds
actions: Present resource, proposed configuration, effort and estimated savings
outputs: A handoff with an implementation and measurement plan

slides.title: Generate reports for a specific audience
slides.takeaway: Acceptance: every headline number retains its period, filters and cost basis.
slides.notes: An engineering report should emphasize owned resources and next actions; a leadership report may emphasize the overall trend and decisions required. The native report formats support those audiences, but visual polish does not verify the arithmetic. Reconcile key totals before distributing the artifact and make assumptions visible. Reports generated by the service are distinct from this documentation package.
inputs: A reporting question, audience and format
Relevant data scope and optional example template
actions: Assemble cost summaries, comparisons and visual artifacts
Revise the report through follow-up requests
outputs: A report artifact ready for human review and distribution

slides.title: Tasks make work and history inspectable
slides.takeaway: Acceptance: inspect the first runs and disable a cadence that produces noise or stale information.
slides.notes: A task is useful when the team needs an inspectable execution record rather than a one-off chat answer. Begin with a report whose source totals have already been reconciled. Give the schedule an owner and a review cadence. A recurring task can continue producing misleading output if its context or source access changes, so inspect failures and data drift.
inputs: An on-demand request or recurring schedule
A bounded analysis/report prompt and destination
actions: Retain task history, results and integration outcomes
outputs: Evidence of what ran and where the output went

slides.title: Anomaly-event automation needs an explicit trigger
slides.takeaway: Acceptance: this documented trigger is not a general automation engine for every cost threshold.
slides.notes: The event-driven workflow builds on Cost Anomaly Detection and an EventBridge rule. The prompt describes the response; the actual monitor and event configuration determine when it runs. Review the generated automation and its destination. Scheduled and event-based Jira actions can be pre-authorized at setup, so enablement is itself an approval decision rather than an expectation of a confirmation prompt for every run.
inputs: Cost Anomaly Detection monitor and matching condition
Configured EventBridge permissions and delivery destination
actions: Run the stored investigation prompt when a matching event arrives
outputs: An investigation task for the event
A configured report, Slack message or Jira handoff

slides.title: Context files and memory make reporting team-specific
slides.takeaway: Business context is interpretive guidance—not access control or an authoritative ledger.
slides.notes: Upload a reviewed account-to-team mapping and the reporting conventions the organization actually uses. Context files are read-only from the agent’s perspective; update the source through the supported management path. Memory can retain preferences, but stale or incorrect preferences need correction. Do not upload secrets or assume an owner field in a context file can change a Jira assignee automatically.

left.title: Context files
left.body: Account ownership, cost categories, report templates and recurring instructions.

right.title: Memory
right.body: Preferences carried into future questions, reports and tasks.

slides.callout: Recommended practice: name a context owner and review date; reconcile labels with the current organization.

slides.title: Collaboration approval depends on action and trigger
slides.takeaway: Do not assume every outbound write prompts for confirmation.
slides.notes: The supported external writes are constrained. Jira issue and comment actions started in chat or on-demand require confirmation; the same actions can be pre-authorized in scheduled or event-based automations. Slack posting does not require a per-message approval prompt. The Slack integration is outbound rather than a channel command bot. Jira support is not general workflow administration and does not allow arbitrary assignee or status updates.
rows: Not a supported action path here
Use the team’s separate delivery process

slides.title: Preview governance is part of the workflow
slides.takeaway: Approve storage, inference and destination boundaries before uploading organizational context.
slides.notes: The preview stores agent data in us-east-1 and can use inference within the originating US geography. Storage location and inference location are different questions. An organization must also approve the content sent to Jira or Slack. Keep role and integration scope narrow and account for underlying service/API consumption. This is a readiness recommendation, not legal or financial advice.

items.title: Data boundary
items.body: us-east-1 storage; US-geography inference during preview.

items.title: Identity
items.body: Separate agent/operator access with only required sources.

items.title: Destinations
items.body: Approved projects and channels; understand pre-authorization.

slides.title: Verify cost totals and implemented follow-up
slides.takeaway: Record implemented engineering actions and verify resulting costs.
slides.notes: Begin with one account group and a known owner. Reconcile an analysis before automating it, investigate a representative anomaly, and send one approved recommendation through the team’s normal change process. Measure reviewer effort, accepted explanations, duplicate or noisy tickets and any independently observed post-change result. The presentation contains all 13 capability entries through the crosswalk below. Questions follow the timed close.

items.title: Week 1
items.body: Approve preview/data scope and reconcile a baseline.

items.title: Weeks 2–3
items.body: Investigate one anomaly and route one low-risk opportunity.

items.title: Week 4
items.body: Review evidence, cost and owner feedback; automate only useful work.
